blocking.section: Decision outcome (Export row) and Confirmation (Environment golden test)
blocking.issue: The fix for the earlier L1-4 cannot be built as written. The ADR says the resource is built with no environment detector, so `OTEL_*` variables are ignored. In OpenTelemetry Go, though, the public `WithResource` option of all three providers merges `resource.Environment()` into the resource it is given. This holds for `sdk/trace` (provider.go), `sdk/metric` (config.go) and `sdk/log` (provider.go), where the code is `cfg.resource, err = resource.Merge(resource.Environment(), r)` (checked on main). Leaving `WithResource` out does not help, because the default is `resource.Default()`, which also reads the environment. So `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` and `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` still add keys to every exported span, metric and log record, even when `internal/telemetry` passes a resource built by hand. Two Nodes on one Revision can then export different resources, which breaks the ADR's 'One configuration source' driver (pack 8.1). The planned golden test that sets `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` and expects a byte-identical resource would fail.
blocking.evidence: Export row: "Providers, processors and exporters get explicit options and the resource no environment detector, so `OTEL_*` process variables are ignored; `${OTEL_...}` render-time substitution stays valid"; Confirmation: "**Environment golden test**, Planned (M1): with `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` set, `ruralzd` exports a byte-identical resource, headers and sampling." Driver: "**One configuration source**: Nodes on one Revision differ only in `secretRef` values and `RURALZ_*` settings (pack section 8.1)."
blocking.fix: Replace the Export row sentence with: '`ruralzd` and `ruralz-control` remove every `OTEL_*` variable from their own process environment (`os.Unsetenv`) at startup, before any SDK constructor runs, because the SDK's `WithResource` always merges `resource.Environment()`. Providers, processors and exporters then take explicit options. `${OTEL_...}` substitution is unaffected, because it runs at render time (`ruralz bundle render`) and file-mode `ruralzd` loads an already rendered Bundle ([Configuration model](../architecture/02-configuration-model.md#environment-substitution)).' Leave the golden test as it is. It now checks this rule, and it SHOULD also assert that `os.Getenv("OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES")` is empty once startup finishes.

blocking.issue: The audit export mechanism resolves L1-2's rule but cannot produce correct records as written. The Exporter's `Export` method takes `[]sdklog.Record`. In `sdk/log`, `Record` has setters for timestamp, severity, body, attributes and trace context. Its `resource` and `scope` fields, however, are unexported and are set only when a Logger emits the record: `Resource()` returns `r.resource`, and no `SetResource` or `SetScope` exists (sdk/log/record.go, checked on main). If the leader 'calls the OTLP log exporter directly' with records it builds itself, every audit record goes out with no resource and no scope. It then loses `service.name`, `service.instance.id` and the Cluster and Environment attributes that the Resource row requires in Control mode. The row also never says how an acknowledgement reaches the Raft high-water mark. `log.Logger.Emit` returns nothing, so records that go through a Logger and a BatchProcessor, the normal path, can never report a failed export.
blocking.evidence: "| Audit export | The Ruralz Control leader calls the OTLP log exporter directly, bypassing `slog` and the drop queues: batches keyed by Raft index, retried until acknowledged, partial success counted as failure; it lags, never drops (TB-12 exception proposed in OQ-observability-19) | Planned (M2) |"; Resource row: "plus Cluster and Environment in Control mode".
blocking.fix: Change the Audit export row to: 'The leader emits each committed entry through a dedicated `sdklog.LoggerProvider` that carries the Resource-row resource and has only a synchronous capture Processor, with no BatchProcessor. The capture Processor clones each record into the current batch. The leader then calls the OTLP log exporter's `Export` itself and advances the high-water mark only when `Export` returns a nil error; the HTTP exporter returns a partial success as an error. Batches are keyed by Raft index, retried until acknowledged, and lag instead of dropping (TB-12 exception proposed in OQ-observability-19).' Extend the Audit export test so that it also asserts the resource attributes on the records the Collector receives.

non_blocking.suggestion: A sequence lock allows only one writer at a time, and concurrent sampled requests can hit the same histogram label set, up to both per-Node caps. As written, a second writer would spin, and that breaks the driver 'no request goroutine waits on a lock'. Add: 'a writer takes the slot with one compare-and-swap of the sequence from even to odd, or skips the exemplar if that fails; readers retry on an odd or changed sequence.'

One worker both owns stdout and feeds the bridge (`wrk --> out`, `wrk --> br`). A blocked stdout pipe therefore also stops OTLP log export, and both streams fall to `queue_full`. Say whether that coupling is intended. If it is not, hand each record to the bridge before the stdout write, or give the stdout write its own small bounded buffer. The wording 'encodes each once for stdout and the bridge' is also loose: the bridge needs a rebuilt `slog.Record` and an `otelslog` conversion. Say that this cost counts toward the 5% CPU row (hypothesis).

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Exemplars row) and More information
non_blocking.suggestion: The exemplar slot, its sequence lock and its memory are not in Observability, and the Cardinality and overhead budgets memory model (300 bytes per histogram label set, about 22.2 MiB of metrics, hypothesis) leaves them out. Add a proposed Observability amendment to More information that adds the slot size (about 64 bytes per histogram label set, hypothesis) to that model. Otherwise the ADR adds a mechanism that its owning document does not describe.

Name the OTLP transport. The owning document's example uses port 4317 (OTLP/gRPC), and the gRPC exporters would link grpc-go into `ruralzd` at M1, although grpc-go's catalog row is Planned (M3). OTLP/HTTP (`otlptracehttp`, `otlpmetrichttp`, `otlploghttp`) avoids that dependency. This remains open from the previous review.
